scenarios.title: Repair the certificate chain for an HTTPS site
scenarios.summary: Use the supplied Apache configuration to restore trusted HTTPS for the reports site while keeping the archive site working.
scenarios.objective: Restore the reports site’s matching certificate name and trusted issuer path for the supplied client. Keep the archive client verifying its original site. Save and apply your configuration, then check both results.
scenarios.retry_guidance: Inspect the failing client and compare its requested name, selected host, certificate and issuer result.

guide.title: Understand the task
guide.why: The first certificate in the configured file identifies the site and is called the leaf. Its listed DNS name must match the name the client intended to contact. The configured key must match the leaf’s public key.

guide.title: Try the separate example
guide.why: The server can supply intermediate certificates after the leaf. A client uses those issuer links to reach an anchor it already trusts. Including a root in the server file cannot make the client trust that root.

guide.title: Complete the independent assignment
guide.why: Save configuration checks the file’s structure. Apply saved configuration checks the supplied file and key pair and updates the active listener. A successful apply can still leave a client unable to verify the name or build the issuer path.
guide.action: Check the saved and applied setup.

scenarios.explanation: Both clients reached their intended servers, matched their DNS names and built issuer paths to their own trust anchors. A matching key lets the listener use the certificate. A supplied intermediate completes the client’s issuer path.
hints: Compare Name to verify and Certificate served in the primary trial. Read the issuer message separately from the DNS name check.
Look for a supplied bundle whose first certificate identifies the reports site and whose next certificate supplies the missing issuer.
The key must match the first certificate’s public key ID. Apply the saved file before rechecking client trials.
scenarios.simplifications: One simulated Apache 2.4.8+ listener with literal names and supplied certificate and key IDs. Client trials use fixed trust anchors, day numbers, exact DNS names and known issuer links. No real files, credentials, browser, network, cryptography or server are used. The exercise omits certificate creation, protocol versions, wildcard names, alternate issuer paths, revocation, encrypted keys and real Apache reload behavior.

scenarios.title: Correct certificate selection on a shared HTTPS listener
scenarios.summary: Restore the correct certificate for each named HTTPS site and preserve the intended default.
scenarios.objective: Make the catalog and docs clients select their matching sites and verify the served certificates. Keep the catalog site as the default for unknown or absent SNI. Save and apply the configuration. The default must still fail the DNS check for an unrelated name.
scenarios.retry_guidance: Inspect the failing client and compare its requested name, selected host, certificate and issuer result.

guide.title: Understand the task
guide.why: Server Name Indication (SNI) is a name the client sends early in the TLS exchange. The listener matches it against ServerName on this shared address and port, then presents the certificate configured in the selected block.

guide.title: Try the separate example
guide.why: A site can be selected by SNI and still present a certificate for the wrong name. Read Selected host and Certificate served, then compare the DNS match and the trust path.

guide.title: Complete the independent assignment
guide.why: In this profile, an unknown or absent SNI uses the first block. That lets the listener present a certificate. It does not make that certificate valid for the unknown name.
guide.action: Check the saved and applied setup.

scenarios.explanation: The named clients used SNI to select the matching blocks, then verified the presented DNS names and trusted paths. The intended first block handled unknown or absent SNI without passing a certificate name check for that unrelated name.
hints: Compare the selected host and the supplied DNS names in the certificate records. A trusted path can appear beside a DNS name mismatch.
Correct the block names or the pairings so each named trial receives a matching certificate and key.
The default site comes from the first block on this listener. Check both unknown-SNI and no-SNI trials.
scenarios.simplifications: One simulated Apache 2.4.8+ listener with literal names and supplied certificate and key IDs. Client trials use fixed trust anchors, day numbers, exact DNS names and known issuer links. No real files, credentials, browser, network, cryptography or server are used. The exercise omits certificate creation, protocol versions, wildcard names, alternate issuer paths, revocation, encrypted keys and real Apache reload behavior.
